(1) MSA accuracy has significantly improved, (2) there are still important limitations, and (3) the future of MSA lies in knowledge-enabled, dynamic approaches.

1) MSA methods have significantly progressed and are now able to identify most of the conserved sequence features that determine a protein family's broad molecular function; 2) however, they fail to align the locally conserved motifs, which reflect functional specificities and that modulate a family's function in a particular cellular context; 3) MSA accuracy is also significantly affected by the quality of the input protein sequences, in particular the presence of poorly aligned, fragmentary and badly predicted sequences
